option.terminology.syntheaYear.help:
During Synthea import, diagnoses, procedures and medications are mapped to German ICD-10-GM, OPS and ATC codes from this year. Codes and descriptions can differ between 2025 and 2026; clinical dates stay the same. Manually entered workbook values are not remapped by this setting.

Warning: The bundled medication profile permits ATC versions up to 2025. ATC 2026 with its year included therefore violates this profile requirement.
option.terminology.syntheaYear.label: Synthea mapping year
option.terminology.versionOutput.help:
Controls version information for codes mapped during Synthea import. Codes and descriptions stay the same.

Catalogue year: Coding.version contains the year used, e.g. “2025”.

Omit: The version is absent. Since the KDS profiles require it for ICD-10-GM, OPS and ATC, validation reports profile errors.

DAR: A Data Absent Reason explains the missing version. It does not establish that the code belongs to a permitted catalogue year. DAR uses the field-specific version rules in the DAR section; without a selected rule, the version is omitted.
option.terminology.versionOutput.label: Coding version

choice.contact-fill-missing: Derive missing encounter assignments from timestamps
choice.contact-timestamp-only: Always derive encounter assignments from timestamps
option.reference.DocumentReference.assig:
Supplied only: Retain supplied encounters. Without an input encounter, leave the reference absent.

Derive missing: Retain supplied encounters and use timestamp matching only when none is supplied. This is the default.

Always derive: Recompute encounters from timestamps, replacing supplied encounters. Without a usable timestamp or matching encounter, omit even supplied references and report the reason.

In the first two modes, retain temporally conflicting encounters and report the conflict. Encounters are identified by the combination of patient ID and case number. If this combination is absent from the input, the nonexistent encounter is reported.

The output end is adjusted afterwards. DAR takes precedence; the final status follows the output end. Resulting inconsistencies between parent and child periods are allowed as test data. Quarter/year end use the start after time shifting. Start + 1 second uses midnight as the calculation basis for a date without a time; otherwise date precision is preserved.

Always: replaces an end supplied in the input as well. Only when the input end is missing: checks the original table value. An internally derived end does not prevent the rule. This choice has no effect when preserving input and derivations.

option.resource.Observation.laboratory.u: Output code in unit instead of code

For UCUM-coded measurements, move the machine-readable code from code to unit and remove code. This produces faulty test data, for example when mmol/L appears only in unit. Applies to valueQuantity and component.valueQuantity. Replaces the readable unit text; value, comparator and system are retained. DAR rules are applied afterwards. FHIR validation may report errors for this output.

app.workbookInspectionHint: Excel: checks sheet structure and column headings. CSV: also checks file groups, record structure and patient assignments using the shared converter. Row counts exclude headers. Further clinical checks run during conversion.
app.syntheaInspectionHint: Inspection counts resources and patients in the JSON bundles. The run imports Synthea R4 data through the selected table format and reports imported and unsupported content. Bundles without patients are skipped.
app.generation.title: Generate Synthea data
app.generation.hint: Seeds determine random sequences. Matching seeds, dates, settings and Synthea version make generation repeatable. KDS output uses the current editor settings.
app.generation.loadFailed: Could not load settings for the installed Synthea version.
app.generation.timestampSeeds: Use the current timestamp as seed
app.generation.timestampSeedsHint: At submission, sets both patient and clinician seeds to the same current Unix timestamp in milliseconds. An entered single-person seed is also replaced when requesting one patient. The values used are saved with the run. When disabled, the entered seeds apply.
app.generation.overflow: Generate additional patients to replace deceased patients
app.generation.selectionHint: The exported patient count can differ from the requested count. Replacing deceased patients can produce additional bundles. Vital status and selection modules restrict accepted patients; unsuitable combinations can reach the attempt limit.
app.generation.modulesHint: No selection: all available modules. Selecting modules restricts disease and care processes; core processes remain active. Info icons explain the effects and show examples.
app.generation.error.minimum: The value must be at least {min}.
app.generation.error.step: Enter a multiple of {step}, for example 100, 200 or 300.
app.generation.error.minAgeOrder: Minimum age must not exceed maximum age.
app.generation.error.maxAgeOrder: Maximum age must not be below minimum age.
app.generation.error.futureDate: Simulation end must not be in the future.
app.generation.error.dateOrder: The reference date must be on or before simulation end.
app.generation.error.seedInteger: Enter an integer seed without decimal places or spaces.
app.generation.error.singlePatient: A single-person seed requires exactly one requested patient. Clear this field or set the patient count to 1.
app.generation.error.state: Choose a state from the list.
app.generation.error.city: Choose a city in the selected state or clear the city selection.
app.datasets.title: Datasets
app.datasets.failed: Could not load the result overview.
app.datasets.incomplete: This run failed. Available datasets and reports support inspection; they do not establish a successful import.
app.datasets.countHint: Counted formats: {formats}. Repeated resource IDs: {repeated}. Resources without IDs: {missing}. Counting is not FHIR validation.
app.datasets.reportCounts: Import issues: {issues} · omitted content: {omissions} · failed cases: {failures} · end derivations: {derivations} · output decisions: {selections} · validation: {errors} errors, {warnings} warnings
app.datasets.fileHint: Files download directly. The complete run ZIP contains all results and reports; dataset ZIPs contain the FHIR files of one configuration.
app.datasets.moreFiles: Showing the first 200 matches. Use search to narrow the selection.
app.datasets.searchRuns: Find runs by input, configuration or status
app.generation.nativeHint: Generates original Synthea FHIR R4 JSON data. The KDS configuration does not apply.
app.upload.title: Load datasets into FHIR servers
app.upload.hint: Select datasets and a target server. Existing resources with the same ID are updated. Conflicting contents within this selection are reported before loading.
app.upload.error: The request could not be completed. Please try again.
app.upload.conflictDetail: {resource} has conflicting contents. Nothing was uploaded. Please change the selection.
app.upload.partial: Some resources may already have been uploaded. The server state was not rolled back.
app.failure.memory: The run failed because memory was exhausted. Generated files may be incomplete. Use less history or smaller inputs and check available memory.
app.failure.killed: The process was forcibly terminated. Memory exhaustion is a possible but unconfirmed cause. Generated files may be incomplete.
app.loadRunHelp: Loads this run’s saved input, generation settings and FHIR configuration into the editor, replacing current settings. Edit them and start a new run when ready.
app.downloadHelp: ZIP with all files still saved for this run and its configuration. After cleanup it contains retained files and checksums; deleted sources and logs are not included.
app.deleteRunConfirm: Delete completely removes the run including its configuration, Excel workbooks and results. Data already uploaded to the FHIR server remain available.
identifier.typeHelp: The list includes identifier types from the bundled FHIR and KDS profiles. System, code and display are editable. All types are available for all selected resources. Multiple codings describe the same identifier type.
dar.onlyWhenMissing: Add DAR only when the value is missing
dar.onlyWhenMissingHelp: Add when missing: Retains existing values and existing DAR after conversion, including derived values. Always replace: Replaces existing values and existing DAR with the selected DAR.
option.stationServiceProvider.label: Ward as service provider
option.stationServiceProvider.help: Uses the ward of the ward/service encounter as an Organization in Encounter.serviceProvider. Its stable ID is based on facility, department and ward. A contained organization is embedded in the Encounter; an external organization can be generated or only referenced.
option.stationLocation.label: Output ward as Location
option.stationLocation.help: Creates the ward Location with physicalType wa. Can be combined with the ward organization. Room and bed can still be represented independently; Location output settings also apply.
identifier.useHelp: FHIR: <ResourceType>.identifier.use, e.g. Patient.identifier.use or Encounter.identifier.use. Describes the use of each identifier added by this rule: usual = customary use, official = official use, temp = temporary, secondary = supplementary, old = no longer valid. Unspecified leaves the field empty. This describes the identifier; it changes neither its value nor the resource selection.
identifier.typeTextHelp: FHIR: <ResourceType>.identifier.type.text, e.g. Patient.identifier.type.text. A free, human-readable description of the kind of identifier, such as “Medical record number” or “Visit number”. It is added to each identifier generated by this rule. The type codings below populate identifier.type.coding; their display text populates coding.display. The type description complements these codings but does not set a type code itself. An empty field is omitted.
app.config.token.openBrace: Inserts {{ into the pattern. The resulting identifier contains a single opening brace {.
app.config.token.closeBrace: Inserts }} into the pattern. The resulting identifier contains a single closing brace }.
identifier.countStartHelp: First number for {count} and zero-padded forms such as {count:08}. All selected resources of a rule share a counter within each conversion, including repetitions. Synthea import and generation convert each patient separately, restarting the counter for each patient. Include {patientId} or {hash} for values that are unique across patients. Without a counter token, the start value has no effect.
app.config.darInherited: The common encounter rule applies. Select a DAR rule here to override it for this encounter class.
app.upload.removeConfirm: Delete this local upload history entry and its logs? Uploaded resources remain on the FHIR server.
app.upload.clearConfirm: Delete all completed local upload history entries and their logs? Active uploads and resources on the FHIR servers are retained.
app.datasets.inputsHint: Compact inputs for conversion from Excel, including version information. Externally referenced document files must be supplied separately.
app.datasets.downloadHint: ZIP containing this dataset’s generated FHIR result files in the selected output formats.
app.cleanup.title: Clean up or delete run
app.cleanup.keep: Clean up: retain configuration, Excel workbooks, FHIR results and required referenced files.
app.cleanup.remove: Remove source data, intermediate files, logs and duplicate ZIP archives. Comparisons against deleted sources can no longer be repeated. Downloads remain available; ZIP archives are recreated on demand.
app.cleanup.replay: Saved Excel workbooks can be downloaded via “Configuration and Excel” and converted again with their saved configuration.
app.replay.help: Reuse all {count} saved Excel workbooks from this run and load its configuration into the editor. Adjust the name, configuration and ID prefix or suffix, then start conversion. Synthea is not executed again. Failed runs may contain only part of the dataset.
app.replay.inputHelp: All workbooks are converted together using the current editor configuration. Synthea is not executed again. The new run saves independent copies of the workbooks.
app.inputRemoveConfirm: Remove “{name}” from saved inputs? Existing runs retain their own copies and results. The original file on your computer is kept.
app.inputRemoveFailed: The input could not be removed.
app.outcomes.transferCounts: {checked} comparisons · {differences} with differences · {notes} import notes · {unavailable} not assessed
app.outcomes.explanation: Import notes document transfer limitations and may identify mapping work. Comparison differences are counted per source dataset and variant; each comparison reports its first difference. {count} notes are covered by disabled resources or DAR replacements and accounted for separately.
app.generation.inpatientOnly: Only patients with an inpatient stay
app.generation.inpatientMinDays: Minimum inpatient stay duration in days
app.generation.inpatientHelp: Keeps patients with at least one inpatient stay that reaches the minimum duration by simulation end and overlaps the exported history period. One day is 24 hours. Other encounters for these patients are also retained. The attempt limit (Advanced generation settings) applies to each requested patient slot.
app.tableFormat.help: CSV generation uses less memory and is faster for larger datasets. Choose Excel to conveniently edit the generated data afterwards. Both table formats can be edited and converted again.
app.diagnostics.help: Compares generated FHIR data with the Synthea source and saves detailed transfer reports. Requires additional time, memory and disk space. Input and conversion errors are reported even when diagnostics are disabled.
app.bulk.modeHelp: Standard run: 1 to 1,000 patients per run. Bulk run: 1 to 100,000 patients in one overall job with sequential subruns and chunks of up to 100 patients. Both modes offer KDS FHIR or original Synthea FHIR. Bulk results are stored as NDJSON Gzip files.
app.bulk.title: Bulk data generation
app.bulk.recommend: We recommend bulk generation for this patient count.
app.bulk.overrides: Bulk mode writes one NDJSON file per subrun, optionally gzip-compressed, with one transaction Bundle per line, with diagnostics disabled regardless of output and validation settings in the configuration editor. Clinical settings still apply. The count refers to generated source patients.
app.bulk.resultsHelp: Each subrun produces one NDJSON file, gzip-compressed by default, with the configured patient count; the last may be smaller. Each line contains a complete FHIR transaction Bundle. Synthea FHIR also includes organizations and clinicians. Files can be downloaded or uploaded to the FHIR server.
app.bulk.deleteHelp: Removes the run, its working files and its local results directory, including all files inside it.
app.bulk.prepare: If memory is low, we recommend stopping running optional services (Data Portal, TORCH, Blaze, HAPI). From the project directory:
app.bulk.restore: After the run, you can restart the previously running services:
app.bulk.memoryReady: Ready: {available} GiB Docker RAM available (at least 3 GiB required).
app.bulk.memoryBlocked: Start blocked: {available} GiB Docker RAM available (at least 3 GiB required).
app.bulk.format: Output: One .ndjson.gz file per subrun with the configured patient count. One complete FHIR transaction Bundle per line.
app.generation.syntheticConsentHelp: Synthea does not generate consent records (Consent). The following consent records are generated: 50% full consent, 15% consent for patient data only, 15% consent for patient and insurance data, 10% full refusal, and 10% without documented consent. Counts are rounded to whole patients, per chunk of up to 100 patients in bulk runs. Date: first inpatient encounter within the configured history, falling back to the first other encounter in that period. Without a matching encounter, the history start is used, but never before birth. Consent is omitted if no plausible date within the patient’s lifetime is available. The distribution is reproducible using the population seed.
app.generation.bulkSeedHelp: Population seed for the first chunk of up to 100 patients. Each subsequent chunk increments it by 1, including across subrun boundaries. The clinician seed stays unchanged. Matching seeds, dates, settings and generator version allow repeatable runs.
app.generation.seedRange: For {patients} patients, {count} seeds from {first} to {last} will be used.
app.bulk.subrunsHelp: Patients per subrun: 100 to 10,000 in steps of 100. Subruns execute sequentially and each produces one NDJSON file, optionally gzip-compressed; the last may be smaller. Generation uses chunks of at most 100 patients, each with the next population seed.
app.bulk.subrunsSummary: One overall job with {count} subruns of at most {size} patients each. All subruns start automatically in sequence.
app.bulk.resumeHelp: Completed 100-patient chunks are retained. The incomplete chunk is regenerated with its original seed, followed by the remaining subruns.
app.bulk.noCopies: Bulk population counts generate new patients. Additional case copies and their per-copy time shifts are disabled. Common time shifts and ID settings still apply.
app.upload.resumeHint: Continues to the same server after the last confirmed patient. Previously uploaded data must still be present on the server. If the server has been cleared, start a new upload.
app.series.help: A series inherits seeds, identifier counters and settings from its last completed block. Continuation requires saved completion counters. Partial 100-patient source blocks are generated in full; unused patients are retained internally for continuation. Previously continued runs lead to their latest successor.
app.series.lockedHelp: Only the additional patient count changes. The backend continues the population seed and counters. The clinician seed and all other settings stay the same. Identifier rules show their next starting values. Complete or resume an unfinished successor first.
app.bulk.fixedFormat: Output format: NDJSON (one transaction Bundle per line)
app.bulk.formatPlain: Output: One .ndjson file per subrun with the configured patient count. One complete FHIR transaction Bundle per line.
app.bulk.checksDisabled: Input diagnostics and FHIR validation are disabled in bulk mode.
app.bulk.outputIntro: Each bulk subrun produces one NDJSON file. Choose whether to compress it with gzip. Set the patients per subrun in the generation settings above.
option.Organization.identity.label: Reuse an organization or create a new one
option.Organization.identity.help: Reuse: The same ward in the same facility and department always uses the same Organization with the same ID, across patients and runs. Create new: Each encounter gets its own Organization with its own ID.
option.Location.identity.label: Reuse a location or create a new one
option.Location.identity.help: Reuse: The same place always uses the same Location with the same ID, across patients and runs. Facility, department and parent locations are included: Bed 1 in Room 101 is a different place from Bed 1 in Room 102. Create new: Each encounter gets its own locations with their own IDs.
option.Medication.identity.label: Reuse a medication or create a new one
option.Medication.identity.help: Reuse: Matching product details use the same Medication with the same ID. Create new: Each request, administration or statement gets its own Medication with its own ID. Requests, administrations and statements remain separate entries.
choice.Organization.identity.separate: Create a new organization for each encounter
choice.Location.identity.separate: Create a new location for each encounter
choice.Medication.identity.separate: Create a new medication for each medication entry
